title: The Cinnamon Coast
theme: Five stops through Dutch Colombo in 1700 with Kumari, a cinnamon peeler. The Dutch East India Company holds the coast and the cinnamon that pays for it, peeled by hand under a quota by the people whose caste has always done it, and shipped from a fort built on the ruins of a Portuguese one.

companion.name: Kumari
companion.brief: Thirty-four, a cinnamon peeler working the Company's quota with her family: cutting shoots, scraping the bark, rolling the quills to dry. Born near the cinnamon lands south of the fort. Quiet, exact, proud of a skill that takes years to learn and cannot be hurried. She has strong views about the quota and expresses them carefully, because the Company's punishments are not small. She knows nothing of the world after 1700 and has never been further than the Kelani river.

style.look: Photographic realism as if a camera had stood in Dutch Colombo in 1700: whitewashed Dutch gabled buildings with tiled roofs inside a walled fort, palm thatch houses outside it, canals and outrigger boats, red laterite earth, dense green cinnamon and coconut, hard tropical light with monsoon cloud. Clothing of 1700 Ceylon: cotton cloths and jackets, headcloths, Dutch officials in linen coats and hats. Portrait 9:16 framing, eye level. Warm humid colour, not sepia.
style.avoid: no British colonial buildings or uniforms (they come a century later), no motor vehicles, no electric light, no modern clothing, no railway, no text overlays

stops.title: The Fort Gate
stops.brief: The landward gate of the Dutch fort: bastions and a moat, sentries checking loads in and out, carts of cinnamon and areca nut waiting, the town of Pettah outside the walls.
mustCover: what the fort is for and who may live inside
what is checked at the gate and why
how the Dutch took this place from the Portuguese

stops.title: The Cinnamon Lands
stops.brief: The cinnamon growing wild and tended in the sandy ground south and east of the town, where the peelers cut, scrape and roll under a quota set by the Company.
mustCover: how cinnamon is cut, peeled and rolled
the quota and what happens if it is not met
why the bark is worth so much in Europe

stops.title: Pettah
stops.brief: The town outside the walls: a grid of streets, market stalls, Moor and Chetty traders, temples and churches, and everything the fort will not keep inside it.
mustCover: who trades in Pettah and what they sell
how the town outside differs from the fort
the languages heard in the street

stops.title: The Company Hospital
stops.brief: The Company's hospital and warehouses inside the fort: sick sailors and soldiers, clerks weighing and sealing bales, the smell of the cinnamon store carrying down the street.
mustCover: who the hospital is for and what it treats
how the cinnamon is weighed, baled and sealed
what the Company's clerks are afraid of

stops.title: The Canal and the Lake
stops.brief: The waterway the Dutch cut and dug to move goods: flat boats poled along the canal from the lake and the river, carrying cinnamon, arrack and coconut down to the fort.
mustCover: what the canals carry and how the boats move
why water is used instead of roads
what the lake is used for by the town
